summary: This program is the bakery's simple menu app: it creates three kinds of cookie objects, prints a description of each one, and then packages the gift cookie with a personal message.

lines.text: Creates a plain cookie by passing its flavor to the Cookie constructor, which stores that flavor inside the new object.
Creates a decorated cookie; because DecoratedCookie extends Cookie, it inherits the flavor handling and adds its own description.
Creates a gift cookie, the subclass that also knows how to package itself for a customer.
Passes the plain cookie to the helper method that prints one menu line.
The same helper accepts a DecoratedCookie because every DecoratedCookie is also a Cookie, which is what inheritance buys you here.
One helper method therefore handles all three cookie types without any if statements about which type it received.
Calls a method that only GiftCookie defines, so it must be called through the gift variable rather than a plain Cookie variable.
Declaring the parameter as the parent type Cookie is what lets this one method serve all three subclasses.
Each object runs its own version of describe(), so the output differs per cookie type even though the calling code is identical; this is polymorphism in action.
